title: SLAC Leads DOE's SPIRE Autonomous Lab Project
source_used: ExecutiveGov; date checked against Tech Times (11 Oct 2026)
key_facts: SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory (US Department of Energy) said Thursday it will lead a multi-institution effort to build an autonomous research platform where AI agents, robots and smart detectors run experiments.
The project is SPIRE, unveiled by the DOE Office of Science at the Golden Age of Science Summit in Washington, alongside new Genesis Mission projects.
Partners: University of Chicago, Stanford University and Argonne, Brookhaven and Lawrence Berkeley national laboratories, with industry advisers.
Three targets: AI-guided robotics for fragile samples, X-ray and electron beams that correct themselves, and data analysis while experiments run.
Detectors at SLAC's upgraded X-ray laser will produce more than a terabyte of data per second, so engineers are embedding AI in detector chips.
In a recent DOE demonstration, AI agents ran a battery imaging workflow, moving data between national laboratories, producing 3D reconstructions and identifying individual particles.
SLAC staff engineer Tim Dunn said the step could take a process that used to take months and reduce it to minutes; hard-wired safety systems remain.
quote_evidence: The Department of Energy's SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory said Thursday it will lead a multi-institution effort to build an autonomous research platform where artificial intelligence agents, robots and smart detectors conduct experiments.
Hard-wired safety systems will remain, with researchers setting scientific objectives and AI operating within those limits.
why_it_matters_hint: Big X-ray facilities produce more data than people can analyse, so DOE is funding a platform where AI agents run the experiments.
event_date: 8 Oct 2026 (Tech Times, 11 Oct 2026: DOE selected SLAC on 8 Oct; ExecutiveGov says 'Thursday')
